in: Create ONE new Java package, com.securityexpert.nexus.ui2.discovery.cp, inside the EXISTING ui2/platform-core module. Do not create a new Gradle subproject: ui2/settings.gradle.kts fixes eleven subprojects and Ui2ArchitectureTest asserts that listing. platform-core is the correct home for a second reason -- direction tests dir1, dir7 and dir10 already forbid it any project dependency, any persistence framework and any Python runtime, which is the structural form of contract rules DI-1 and the know-how-only language rule.

Candidate classification, contract section 4. A CandidateKind type carrying K-1 to K-10 exactly as the section 4.2 table defines them, plus the two outcomes UNCLASSIFIED and AMBIGUOUS. A classifier that decides kind from object type and the three flags PRODUCT, VIRT_HOST, VIRT_SYSTEM and from nothing else (CL-1). An unmeasured flag combination yields UNCLASSIFIED and is returned, never dropped and never assigned to the nearest kind (CL-2). A combination matching more than one kind yields AMBIGUOUS and is never resolved by preference order (CL-2). The flag set is closed at exactly three (CL-4).

Host resolution, contract section 5.1. A pure function of the two address fields -- management address and own address -- returning exactly one of the three HR-1/HR-2/HR-3 outcomes. HR-2 covers the empty own address as the same case as a differing one, not as a separate rule and not as a value to repair. HR-3 yields NOT_APPLICABLE, never UNKNOWN. HR-4 is a hard constraint on the implementation: this function must NOT branch on object type or on candidate kind. Equality is decided by comparing the two values locally after trimming surrounding whitespace and after nothing else -- no numeric casting, no zero-stripping, no truncation or padding, no case or punctuation normalization. Where equality cannot be decided this way the outcome is NOT_EVALUABLE.

Host linking, contract section 5.2. For a candidate resolved by HR-2, find the candidates in the SAME owning domain whose own address equals its management address. Exactly one match links; zero yields MISSING; more than one yields AMBIGUOUS (HL-1). In the MISSING and AMBIGUOUS cases NO host identifier is recorded. A resolved link is recorded by the host candidate's stable identifier, never by the address (HL-2). Candidates with MISSING or AMBIGUOUS hosts are still returned (HL-3).

Member-to-cluster resolution, contract section 5.3. The cluster reference's stable identifier is the join key. The display name is never compared, never used as a key and never used to break a tie (MC-1). Where the reference is absent, or carries a display name but no identifier, the result is NOT_EVALUABLE with NO fallback of any kind (MC-2). The tree is built from the member side only; a cluster with no referencing member is a cluster with no known members, not an empty cluster (MC-3).

The candidate row, contract section 6. The fields of the 6.2 table, with the per-kind presence the table states and with CR-0 honoured: a '?' cell means the field MAY BE ABSENT and the code handles the absence -- it is never treated as present. The candidate key is the pair (owning domain, stable identifier) per CR-1, because U-1 is unsettled. The stable identifier is opaque: not cast, not trimmed of leading zeroes, not normalized, not parsed (CR-1). Owning domain comes from the enumeration context, not from the object (CR-5). Candidate kind is derived, never supplied (CR-6). CR-3a: an address on a cluster-kind candidate is never resolved through HL-1 and is never presented as a device address. CR-8a/CR-8b/CR-9: model and software version are never inherited from host to virtual system and a cluster object's are never presented as a member's. CR-11 to CR-14: no field derived from a name, no liveness field, no raw response, no collected device state.

One isolated field-binding site, contract section 6.4 as discharged by the FROZEN status block. A single class or single enum is the ONLY place where a role name is associated with a concrete management-API field name. Every entry is marked UNVERIFIED, because the measurement lived in a Product Owner session against a management server no worker has. Every rule in the classification and resolution code is written against the ROLE names, so that no rule depends on a concrete field name. A role that cannot be bound is recorded UNKNOWN and its field is not carried (FB-3).

JUnit tests implementing contract section 9 checks 8, 10, 12 and 13 over synthetic fixtures constructed in the test source. Check 8, name-blindness: classify a fixture set twice, once as built and once with EVERY display-name field replaced by one constant, and assert the kind assignment, every host resolution and every cluster link are identical. Check 10, type-blindness: assert host resolution computed with no access to object type produces the same outcome for every candidate as the same computation with object type available. Check 12, identifier-only join: assert links are recorded by identifier; assert a run with every cluster display name replaced by a constant produces identical links; assert a run with the identifier removed from every cluster reference produces ZERO links and NOT_EVALUABLE, never a name-based fallback. Check 13, liveness vocabulary: assert that no field name and no enumerated field value anywhere in the produced candidate row belongs to the vocabulary up, down, online, offline, reachable, unreachable, healthy, unhealthy or a synonym -- implement this by reflecting over the candidate row type and its enums, so it keeps holding for fields added later, not by listing today's fields.
Fixtures are synthetic and invented in the test source. No real address, object name, domain name, identifier, serial or certificate subject appears in any file.
out: The transport layer, contract section 3. No HTTP client, no session management, no login, no domain enumeration call, no object query call, no connection-table read, no network code of any kind. This movement compiles and tests without any server and must contain nothing that would try to reach one. That layer is the NEXT movement.
The connection-table channel state of contract section 7.4. It arrives with the transport that reads it; nothing about CS-1 to CS-6 is implemented here.
Persistence of any kind. No repository, no entity, no migration, no SQL. DI-1 says a discovery run writes nothing, and dir7 already forbids platform-core a persistence framework.
Any HTTP surface, any REST controller, any screen, any frontend change. The operator screen is deferred by contract section 11.
Import, deduplication and reconciliation against existing device rows. Contract section 8 fixes the boundary; DI-6 says discovery makes no claim about whether a candidate is already imported.
Any device contact by any transport. Any Palo Alto code. Any change to a FROZEN contract. Any new Gradle subproject. Any change to project/*.json. Any change to the existing Python.
Closing any of the twelve UNKNOWNs of contract section 10, or marking any binding entry VERIFIED.
